name: GHOUL

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Ghoul
Most societies forbid humans to knowingly feed on other
humans. To do so invites a horrid curse: transformation
into a ghoul.
Ghouls are corpse-eaters, shunned for their unspeakable
appetites. They prowl graveyards, breaking into tombs
and digging up coffins to get at the choice morsels within.
Eternally hungry, ghouls eat any flesh, no matter how
rancid or putrid. However, when given the choice, they
favor fresh meat pulled from the bones of children.
A ghoul adopts the likeness of the last creature it ate. As
its unholy appetite grows, it reverts to its usual gaunt and
sickly form, its crusted maw filled with pointed black teeth
and a forked, sore-ridden tongue.
Ghouls speak the Common Tongue.
GHOUL DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 frightening monster
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 40; Insanity 5; Corruption 4
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease or poison; diseased, poisoned
Fear of the Gods A ghoul makes attack rolls with 1 bane
against a creature wearing or wielding a holy symbol.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws and Teeth (melee) +3 with 1 boon (2d6 + 3 plus
Drink Blood on attack roll 20+)
Drink Blood If the target is a living creature of flesh and
blood, it takes 1d6 extra damage and becomes fatigued
for 1 minute. While fatigued in this way, the target is
also slowed. If it was already fatigued, it instead takes
another 1d6 extra damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Unholy Feast The ghoul eats one dead creature it can
reach, which requires concentrating for 1 minute. At
the end of this time, the ghoul utterly consumes the
corpse and assumes the creature’s appearance for 24
hours. While wearing this new form, the ghoul loses its
frightening trait.

name: GIANT

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Giant
Giants are primitive, backward, and incredibly stupid.
They pay little attention to where they go and leave a trail
of smashed houses, flattened wagons, and partly eaten
livestock when wandering through settled lands.
A typical giant stands about 15 feet tall and weighs about
2,000 pounds. It looks like an enormous human with a
slouched posture and exaggerated features: a broad nose,
drooping eyebrows, and a slack mouth filled with stained
teeth the size of shields. Most giants eschew clothing,
though the more modest might strap livestock, living or
dead, over their nether regions, or don carnival tents.
Giants speak the Trollish language. More intelligent
giants might also know the Common Tongue.
GIANT DIFFICULTY 100
Size 3 or larger giant
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 15; Health 100; Insanity 1; Corruption 2
Strength 17 (+7), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 12
Stupidity A giant makes Intellect attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane. Creatures make attack rolls against the
giant’s Intellect with 1 boon.
Crushing Footfalls When a giant moves into a space
occupied by a creature on the ground, the creature must
make an Agility challenge roll. On a failure, it takes 3d6
damage and falls prone. If it’s already prone, it takes 1d6
extra damage. A creature makes this roll once per round
per giant regardless of how many times the giant moves
through its space.
Giantfall The giant deals damage equal to 2d6 × its Size to
everything in the area where it falls. A creature can make
an Agility challenge roll with a number of banes equal
to the giant’s Size (minimum 1 bane). On a success, the
creature takes half the damage and moves to the nearest
open space outside the area. On a failure, the creature
becomes trapped under the giant’s body.
		 A trapped creature is prone, blinded, immobilized, and
totally covered. It can use an action to make an Agility
challenge roll with a number of banes equal to the giant’s
Size + 1. On a success, the creature moves to the nearest
open space and removes all afflictions imposed by Giantfall.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +7 with 3 boons (5d6)
Boulder (long range) +7 with 1 boon (3d6)

name: GOBLIN

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Goblin
Cast out from the realms of faerie long ago, goblins now
make their way in the mortal world. They occupy the
bottom rung of the social ladder, performing the work no
one else is willing to do. Many goblins delight in making
mischief, and the worst of their kind live as thieves,
scoundrels, and troublemakers.
Goblins reproduce like rats. They live in crowded
conditions in underground warrens, often in human cities,
using scraps and stolen materials. No two goblins are exactly
alike. Most stand around 3 feet tall and weigh about 40 or 50
pounds, but all have a unique characteristic that sets them
apart. Horns, fangs, snouts, tails, blotchy skin, extra digits or
eyes, and worse mar their forms.
Goblins speak the Common Tongue and Elvish.
GOBLIN DIFFICULTY 1
Size 1/2 faerie
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 14 (soft leather); Health 8; Insanity 1; Corruption 1
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Iron Vulnerability A goblin is impaired while it is in contact
with iron.
Sneaky A goblin attempting to hide or move silently makes
the Agility challenge roll with 1 boon.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Spear (melee) +3 (1d6)
Bow (long range) +3 (1d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS

originalText:
Golem
Golems are massive, lumbering beings formed from clay
and animated by magic to serve their creators. Prized for
their great strength and their obedience, golems carry
out whatever instructions they receive to the letter. A
golem might spend a century digging a tunnel through a
mountain or stand guard for a thousand lifetimes without
growing tired or feeling the need to do anything else. Each
golem abides by a list of three rules, unique to itself, that its
maker has inscribed inside its head.
GOLEM DIFFICULTY 500
Size 2 or 3 construct
Perception 7 (–3); darksight
Defense 21; Health 200; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 18 (+8), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 8; Unstoppable Advance
Immune damage from cold, disease, and poison; all
afflictions. A golem ignores all banes on rolls it makes.
Damage Resistance A golem takes half damage from fire
and weapons.
Spell Defense A golem takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon.
A creature attacking the golem with a spell makes its
attack roll with 1 bane.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +8 with 3 boons (4d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The golem attacks twice with its fist.
END OF THE ROUND
Unstoppable Advance The golem moves up to its Speed.

name: GORGON

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Gorgon
The Witch-King created the gorgons from his brides, whose
beauty was unmatched by any in the world. He gifted
them with eternal life, but to keep their vanity in check, he
also cursed them, transforming them into monstrosities
whose gaze turned the living to stone statues. Somehow,
the gorgons survived the Witch-King’s defeat and scattered
across the Empire’s lands.
An echo of the beauty that earned their place as the
Witch-King’s brides still lingers in gorgons’ shapely upper
bodies and striking features. But the rest of their forms are
monstrous: crowns of eyeless serpents emerge from their
heads and long serpent tails replace their legs.
Gorgons dwell in old ruins, under cities, or in remote
wilderness areas where they pass the endless years in
isolation. Some offer guidance to mortals who dare
approach, conferring on them the wisdom accumulated
over their long lives.
A gorgon’s gaze retains power for 1d6 days after the
gorgon dies, provided its eyes remain intact. A creature
wielding the gorgon’s head can subject others to the
gorgon’s Petrifying Appearance and Petrifying Gaze.
Gorgons communicate in High Archaic.
GORGON DIFFICULTY 500
Size 1 monster
Perception 17 (+7); darksight
Defense 18; Health 120; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 16 (+6), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 17 (+7)
Speed 8
Immune charmed, compelled, dazed, frightened, stunned
Petrifying Appearance On first seeing a gorgon, a creature
must make a Will challenge roll with 2 banes. On a failure,
the creature gains 1 Insanity, cannot avert its eyes from the
gorgon, and becomes slowed for a number of rounds equal
to the creature’s Insanity total. Whether it gets a success or a
failure, it cannot again be affected by that gorgon’s Petrifying
Appearance until after that creature completes a rest.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Scimitar (melee) +6 with 3 boons (2d6 + 1)
Longbow (long range) +6 with 3 boons (2d6 + 1)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Twin Strike The gorgon attacks twice with its scimitar
or longbow. It makes each attack roll with 1 bane.
Serpent Hair The gorgon uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to attack with the serpents crowning
its head. One target creature within the gorgon’s reach
must make an Agility challenge roll with 1 bane, or
with 3 banes if it averted its eyes. On a failure, the
target takes 2d6 damage, becomes poisoned for
1 minute, and cannot avert its eyes for 1 round.
If the target is already poisoned in this way, it
instead takes 2d6 extra damage.
END OF THE ROUND
Epic Recovery The gorgon removes one
affliction from itself.
Petrifying Gaze Each creature within medium range of the
gorgon that can see it must either use a triggered action
to avert its eyes from the gorgon or make a Strength
challenge roll with 1 bane. For 1 round, a creature that
averts its eyes makes attack rolls with 2 banes, and other
creatures make attack rolls against it with 2 boons.
		 A creature that gets a failure on the Strength challenge
roll takes 4d6 + 20 damage and becomes slowed for
1 minute. If the creature is already slowed, it instead
becomes immobilized. A creature that is incapacitated
by this damage dies instantly, transformed into a stone
statue.
Epic Adversary Roll 1d3 + 1 to determine how many actions
the gorgon can use during the next round. The gorgon can
use these actions during any turn and can do so before its
enemies act. Each time the gorgon uses an action, it can
move up to its Speed before or after the action.

Grave Thrall
Grave thralls haunt old battlefields, clinging to the mortal
world to complete some unfinished task. Their bodies are
worm-eaten, with tattered bits of skin hanging from their bones
and blue pinpricks of light glowing in their empty eye sockets.
Grave thralls do not speak, though they understand those
who have the power to command them.

Insanity —; Corruption 1
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 10
Immune damage from cold, disease, and poison; asleep,
diseased, fatigued, poisoned
Sunlight Weakness A grave thrall is impaired while in an
area lit by sunlight.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Sword (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Great Cat
Great cats such as lions, pumas, and tigers are skilled
hunters, making them more dangerous than other animals
of their size. They wait for prey to draw near and pounce to
take it down quickly.
GREAT CAT DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 or 2 animal
Perception 15 (+5); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 50; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws and Teeth (melee) +4 with 1 boon (3d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Pounce The great cat moves up to its Speed and attacks
twice with its claws and teeth, dealing 1d6 extra damage
on each success. Once the great cat makes this attack, it
cannot do so again for 1 round.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Swift Attack When a creature within the great cat’s reach
moves, the great cat can use a triggered action to attack
the triggering creature with its claws and teeth.

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Gremlin
Cunning mischief-makers, gremlins delight in creating
chaos. Their mere presence causes even the best-laid
plans to go awry. Gremlins followed the goblins out of the
Hidden Kingdoms and now wreak havoc on human cities.
Explosions, misfires, and constructs that behave erratically
are all signs of a gremlin infestation.
Technology attracts gremlins. A gremlin wants nothing
more than to take a device apart to see how it works. When
it puts it back together again, though, the item never seems
to work quite right and has a tendency to break at the most
inopportune times.
Gremlinsaretiny human-shapedcreatureswith grayskin
andspindlybodies,standing8inchestallandweighingnomore
thanapoundortwo.Theyoftenhaveonefeatureof unusual
size,suchasatooth,ear,or nose.Most gremlinsforgoclothing.
Gremlins speak Elvish.
GREMLIN DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1/4 faerie
Perception 13 (+3); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 5; Insanity 3; Corruption 1
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Spell Defense A gremlin takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A
creature attacking the gremlin with a spell makes the
attack roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability A gremlin is impaired while it is in
contact with iron.
Vexing Presence Each creature that is not a faerie and is
within short range of the gremlin makes attack rolls and
challenge rolls with 1 bane.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee) +5 with 1 boon (1 plus Curse)
Curse If the target is not a faerie, it must make a Will
challenge roll with 3 banes. On a failure, the target
becomes cursed for 1 minute. While cursed, whenever
the target makes an attack roll or a challenge roll, it must
roll twice and use the lower number.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Jinx The gremlin uses an action or a triggered action on its
turn to choose one target object within short range of it that
is neither worn nor carried. The target takes 1d6 damage.
Break When a creature within short range of the gremlin
makes an attack roll using a weapon that is not enchanted,
the gremlin can use a triggered action to make an Intellect
challenge roll. On a success, the triggering weapon takes
damage equal to its Health and breaks.

are all signs of a gremlin infestation.
Technology attracts gremlins. A gremlin wants nothing
more than to take a device apart to see how it works. When
it puts it back together again, though, the item never seems
to work quite right and has a tendency to break at the most
inopportune times.
Gremlinsaretiny human-shapedcreatureswith grayskin
andspindlybodies,standing8inchestallandweighingnomore
thanapoundortwo.Theyoftenhaveonefeatureof unusual
size,suchasatooth,ear,or nose.Most gremlinsforgoclothing.
Gremlins speak Elvish.
GREMLIN DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1/4 faerie
Perception 13 (+3); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 5; Insanity 3; Corruption 1
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Spell Defense A gremlin takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A
creature attacking the gremlin with a spell makes the
attack roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability A gremlin is impaired while it is in
contact with iron.
Vexing Presence Each creature that is not a faerie and is
within short range of the gremlin makes attack rolls and
challenge rolls with 1 bane.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee) +5 with 1 boon (1 plus Curse)
Curse If the target is not a faerie, it must make a Will
challenge roll with 3 banes. On a failure, the target
becomes cursed for 1 minute. While cursed, whenever
the target makes an attack roll or a challenge roll, it must
roll twice and use the lower number.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Jinx The gremlin uses an action or a triggered action on its
turn to choose one target object within short range of it that
is neither worn nor carried. The target takes 1d6 damage.
Break When a creature within short range of the gremlin
makes an attack roll using a weapon that is not enchanted,
the gremlin can use a triggered action to make an Intellect
challenge roll. On a success, the triggering weapon takes
damage equal to its Health and breaks.

name: HAG

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Hag
Nymphs are wilderness faerie of surpassing beauty.
But when a nymph’s joy becomes sorrow and bitterness
replaces happiness, hate causes the nymph’s beauty to
wither and die. What’s left is a horror called a hag. Green-
skinned and warty, it is a monstrous reflection of the
nymph’s former self, intent on making everyone else as
miserable as itself.

---

Bestiary
Hags live in dark, foreboding forests, wastelands, and
other desolate areas. They creep through the night hours,
luring children from their beds and stealing them away.
Their vile magic withers crops, sickens livestock, spoils
milk, and brings bad luck.
Hags speak Elvish.
HAG DIFFICULTY 500
Size 1 horrifying faerie
Perception 16 (+6); shadowsight
Defense 19; Health 80; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 16 (+6), Will 16 (+6)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease; asleep, charmed, dazed,
diseased, stunned
Spell Defense A hag takes half damage from spells and makes
any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A creature
attacking the hag with a spell makes the attack roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability A hag is impaired when in contact with iron.
Mind-Bending Horror A creature that gains Insanity
from seeing a hag also becomes compelled while it is
frightened in this way.
See Magic A hag sees auras around creatures, objects, and
places affected by magic.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws (melee) +5 with 3 boons (4d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The hag attacks twice with its claws.
Accursed Eye The hag uses an action or a triggered action
on its turn to make a Will attack roll against the Strength
of one target creature it can see within medium range of
it. On a success, the target becomes impaired for 1 minute.
Accursed Sleep The hag makes a Will attack roll against
the Strength of one target impaired creature it can see
within medium range of it. On success, the target falls
asleep for 1 minute. At the end of this time, the hag can
use a triggered action if it is within medium range of
the target to make a Will attack roll against the target’s
Will. On a success, the target remains asleep for as long
as the hag wishes or until the hag is incapacitated.
Wychfire The hag hurls a ball of green fire at one target
creature within medium range of it, making a Will attack
roll against the target’s Agility. On a success, the target
takes 6d6 damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Change Shape The hag uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to transform into a young human
man or woman of a pleasing appearance. While in
this form, the hag loses its horrifying trait and cannot
use Streaming Smoke; it can use its other attacks and
talents. It remains in this form until it uses a triggered
action at any time to return to its normal form.
Streaming Smoke The hag uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to transform its body into a roiling
cloud of smoke, fly up to its Speed, and then resume its
normal form. While in this form, the hag is immune to all
damage, can move freely through openings wide enough
to permit the passage of air, and can move through
spaces occupied by other creatures.
MAGIC
Power 4
Curse hex (5), frighten (2), weakness (2), swine (1)
Enchantment presence (5), bewitch (2), charm (2), compel (2)
Forbidden harm (5), hateful defecation (2), tongue rip (2),
desire’s end (1), soul exchange (1)
END OF THE ROUND
Epic Recovery The hag removes one affliction from itself.
Epic Adversary Roll 1d3 + 1 to determine how many actions
the hag can use during the next round. The hag can use
these actions during any turn and can do so before its
enemies act. Each time the hag uses an action, it can
move up to its Speed before or after the action.

name: HALFLING

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Halfling
Halflings are diminutive farmers living on the outskirts of
human cities. Their idyllic communities, neat and orderly,
produce much of the foodstuffs on which human nations
depend. Halflings pride themselves in their work, live simply,
and have few ambitions beyond enjoying the time afforded
to them. They are fiercely independent and self-sufficient.
Halflings are cousins to humans, similar in all ways except
height. They stand about 3 feet tall and weigh about 50 pounds.
Halflings have the same range of coloration that humans have.
Halflings speak the Common Tongue.

---

Bestiary
HALFLING DIFFICULTY 1
Size 1/2 halfling
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 14 (hard leather, small shield); Health 10;
Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Spear (melee) +1 (1d6)
Bow (long range) +1 (1d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Good Fortune Whenever a creature within short range of the
halfling rolls a 1 on any die, the halfling can use a triggered
action to let the creature ignore the roll and roll again.
Uncommon Courage When the halfling becomes
frightened, it can use a triggered action to make a Will
challenge roll. On a success, it removes the frightened
affliction.

name: HARPY

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Harpy
Sweet, alluring voices call travelers to their destruction.
They belong to the harpies, a hideous race of accursed
faerie that despise mortals and feed on any they get in
their grasp. Harpies have the wings, tails, and talons of
ravens merged with the torso of nymphs. Beneath the
feces, blood, and hateful behavior, harpies are quite
beautiful.
The harpies were once the loveliest of the nymphs, but
with great beauty came great vanity. They believed they
were greater and more alluring than the Faerie Queen
herself. The Faerie Queen, upon hearing of their boasting,
dismissed them from her court and sent them flying away
as ravens, whose shape still disfigures their forms.
Harpies speak Elvish.
HARPY DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 faerie
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 30; Insanity 3; Corruption 3
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 10; flier (swoop)
Iron Vulnerability A harpy is impaired while it is in contact
with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Talons and Teeth (melee) +5 with 2 boons (3d6 plus
Painful Compulsion)
Painful Compulsion If living, the target must make a Will
challenge roll. On a failure, it becomes compelled for as
long as the harpy concentrates. On a success, it becomes
immune to that harpy’s Painful Compulsion until that
creature completes a rest.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Seductive Song The harpy uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to begin singing. It continues to sing
for 1 round and can take only triggered actions during
that time. Each creature that is within or that moves into
long range of a singing harpy must make a Will challenge
roll, with 1 bane for each singing harpy within range
beyond the first.
On a failure, the creature gains 1 Insanity and becomes
charmed for a number of rounds equal to its Insanity
total. While charmed in this way, the creature must take
the first turn it can each round and use an action to
rush toward the nearest singing harpy by the shortest
available route. Once the creature is within short range
of a singing harpy, it stops moving and becomes stunned
until it is no longer charmed.
		 On a success or after removing the charmed affliction,
the creature becomes immune to all harpies’ Seductive
Song until after it completes a rest.
Harvester
Harvesters haunt the Empire’s oldest cities. Direct
descendants of some ancient society, most likely struck
down by offended gods, they perpetuate their existence by
stealing what they need from humans. When something
breaks in a harvester’s body, it replaces the defective
part with whatever it can take until it looks like it has
been cobbled together from a dozen or more creatures.
Harvesters hide their grotesqueness behind heavy clothing
to help them move among their victims without attracting
attention to themselves.

Size 1 horrifying harvester
Perception 14 (+4); shadowsight
Defense 12; Health 30; Insanity —; Corruption 3
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 14 (+4), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 12
ATTACK OPTIONS
Scalpel (melee) +2 with 2 boons (2d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Extract Organ The organ filch steals an organ from a target
incapacitated or defenseless living creature within its
reach, killing the creature instantly. The filch gains a 2d6
bonus to Health until it completes a rest.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Skittering Dance The filch uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to move up to its Speed. This
movement does not trigger free attacks.
Organ filches scour the shadowed streets of densely
populated cities for vagrants from which they harvest
fresh parts to replace their failing organs. They open up
their victims with long scalpels and carry bottles filled
with preservative fluid to hold their harvests until they
can return to their lairs and install the stolen flesh in their
bodies.
An organ filch goes about covered by a hooded canvas
cloak that is stained with blood from previous hunts.
Beneath is a ghastly figure wrapped in snug linens and
wearing elaborate headgear fitted with lenses to help it
perform surgery.
Organ filches speak High Archaic.

name: TEAR THIEF

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
TEAR THIEF DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 horrifying harvester
Perception 14 (+4); darksight
Defense 17; Health 40; Insanity —; Corruption 4
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 17 (+7), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12
Immune blinded
ATTACK OPTIONS
Long Knife (melee) +7 with 2 boons (3d6 plus Extract Tears)
Extract Tears If living, the target must make a Will
challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure, it gains 1 Insanity
and the tear thief heals 1d6 damage. If the total of the
challenge roll is 0 or lower, the tear thief also plucks out
one of the target’s eyes.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The tear thief can attempt
to hide when it is in an area at least partially
obscured by shadows, even if it is being
observed.
Skittering Dance The tear thief uses an action
or a triggered action on its turn to move
up to its Speed. This movement does not
trigger free attacks.
Harvesters discovered that replacing every part
of their bodies numbed their ability to feel and to
experience emotion. After extensive study, they learned to
concoct an elixir made from human tears that lets them
feel again, if only for a short while. Tear thieves extract
tears by causing their victims to experience horrific pain.
A tear thief wears black leather clothing along with a
heavy coat, white gloves, a top hat, and black lenses over its
eyes. It carries a thin knife with a serrated edge designed to
maximize the victim’s suffering.
Tear thieves speak High Archaic.

name: HELL SWINE

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Hell Swine
Hell swine are a breed of ill-tempered hogs that grow to
obscene size. Vicious and temperamental, they destroy
their habitats and kill just about anything they can catch.
Hell swine have thick, leathery hides, gleaming red eyes,
and tufts of black hair rising from their backs. They gore
their foes with their sharp tusks.
Beastmen have had some success in training hell swine
to serve as steeds, though the beasts are unreliable and can
turn on riders with no warning.
HELL SWINE DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 animal
Perception 9 (–1); shadowsight
Defense 16; Health 60; Insanity 2; Corruption 0
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12
Ferocious When a hell swine would become incapacitated, roll
a d6. On a roll of 5 or 6, the swine instead heals 10 damage.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Tusks (melee) +6 with 2 boons (3d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Vicious Rebuke When the hell swine takes damage, it can
use a triggered action to attack a randomly determined
creature with its tusks.

name: HOBGOBLIN

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Hobgoblin
Cousins to the exiled goblins, hobgoblins remain in the
hidden kingdoms of the faerie, where they live as slaves to
the elf lords and ladies. They are given to frequent bouts
of madness that manifest as random acts of senseless
violence, and often fight on the front lines in defense of the
faerie realms.
Unlike goblins, who have wildly varied appearances,
hobgoblins are identical, regardless of gender. Each one
stands exactly 5 feet, 4½ inches tall and weighs 166 pounds.
All have thick bellies, spindly limbs, and heavy jowls that
hang to their shoulders.
Hobgoblins speak Elvish.
HOBGOBLIN DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1 faerie
Perception 10 (+0); shadowsight
Defense 15 (brigandine, large shield); Health 23; Insanity 1;
Corruption 0
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Iron Vulnerability A hobgoblin is impaired while it is in
contact with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Cleaver (melee) +3 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)

---

Bestiary
END OF THE ROUND
Frenzy If the hobgoblin is not in a frenzy, roll a d6. On
a roll of 6, the hobgoblin goes into a frenzy that lasts
for 1 minute. Until the frenzy ends, the hobgoblin deals
1d6 extra damage with its attacks and is immune to the
frightened affliction, and other creatures make attack
rolls against it with 1 boon.

name: HOOD

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Hood
Hoods were created by a secret society known as the Cabal
of the Black Sun, a largely forgotten group of dark wizards
set on finding immortality. They employ hoods as spies,
thieves, and assassins.
Hoods haunt city streets on fell errands for their
inscrutable masters. They don heavy black cloaks that
seem to drink the light and render them nearly invisible
when in shadows or darkness. They say little and seem
skilled in magic.
The few who have managed to see a hood clearly report it
has craggy features covered by a thick mustache and beard,
much like a dwarf. Only removing their cloaks reveals the
awful truth about hoods’ nature. Rather than skulls, they
have great glass orbs filled with murky liquid. Lamprey-
like creatures swim inside the glass vessels, presumably
controlling the hoods’ actions.
Hoods speak High Archaic.
HOOD DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1/2 monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 15 (hard leather); Health 30; Insanity 3; Corruption 1
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Long Knife (melee) +3 with 2 boons (2d6)
Dagger (melee or short range) +3 with 2 boons (1d6)
Hand Crossbow (medium range) +3 with 2 boons (1d6 plus
Shadow Poison)
Shadow Poison The target must make a Strength
challenge roll. On a failure, it becomes poisoned for 1
minute. While poisoned in this way, the target is also
blinded. If it was already poisoned, it just takes 3d6
extra damage instead.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The hood can attempt to hide when it is
in an area at least partially obscured by shadows, even if
it is being observed.
Shadow Step When the hood is in an area obscured
by shadows or darkness, it can use an action or use
a triggered action on its turn to teleport to another
area obscured by shadows or darkness within medium
range.
MAGIC
Power 1
Shadow nightfall blade (2), darkness (1), shadow dart (1)

originalText:
Jack-o'-Lantern
Glowing wisps flicker and dance across the moors. From a
distance, they look like torches or lanterns, but at close range
they are revealed to be nothing of the sort but in fact plumes
of pale fire that bob in the air. When a living creature comes

name: KILLING MIST

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Killing Mist
Fogplaystricksonthesenses.Sometimestheshadowglimpsed
fromthecorneroftheeyeisnothingmorethana harmless
illusionbroughtonbytheshiftingclouds.Sometimes,though,
there’sreasontoheed thepricklingofthehairsonthebackof
theneck,thecolddreadspreadingthrough theguts,and the
certaintythatthereissomethingelseinthemist—something
utterlymalevolentandnot ofthisworld.
Killing mist appears as a great bank of red-tinged fog that
spills over the ground, plunging the world into pale gloom
as it creeps along. In its depths one can make out weird,
distorted images of impossible shapes accompanied by mad
laughter and strings of words in a deep, muttering voice.
The killing mist never lingers long, dissipating almost as
quickly as it appeared. In the clearing air, one might spot a
few pale, dry bones, all that remains of the unlucky victims
of the entity’s repast.
Killing mist typically conceals itself inside a larger bank
of mundane fog, looking like a particularly dense region of
mist. It haunts shorelines and the surface of waters where
doldrums are common.
KILLING MIST DIFFICULTY 250
Size 10 frightening undead
Perception 20 (+10); sightless
Defense 5; Health 100; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength —, Agility 5 (–5), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 6 (–4)
Speed 6; flier, Flowing Fog
Immune damage from cold, disease, and poison; asleep,
blinded, charmed, dazed, diseased, fatigued, frightened,
poisoned, prone, stunned, and any effect that would
change the killing mist’s shape
Misty Form A killing mist takes half damage from weapons
and double damage from fire. It makes challenge rolls
to resist Fire spells with 1 bane. Other creatures can
move through and end their movement in its space. The
killing mist totally obscures its area. A killing mist ignores
difficult terrain and can move freely through openings
wide enough to permit the passage of air, but it treats
liquid water as a solid object.
		 Once per round, when exposed to wind created by
magic, the mist takes 4d6 damage and is moved 1d6
yards in the direction the wind is blowing.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Feed Each creature within the killing mist’s space must
make a Strength challenge roll with 3 banes. On a failure,
the creature takes 6d6 + 5 damage and becomes fatigued
for 1 minute. While fatigued this way, the creature is
slowed. If it is already fatigued from some other source, it
becomes slowed and takes 2d6 extra damage.
END OF THE ROUND
Flowing Fog Roll a d6. On an even number, the mist moves
a number of yards equal to the roll in a direction of its
choice.
Bewildering Mist Each living creature within the mist’s
space must make a Will challenge roll. On a failure,
the creature gains 1 Insanity and becomes dazed for
1 round. A creature driven mad by the mist also becomes
defenseless until the madness ends.

originalText:
Large Spider
Many breeds of large spider exist in the world, ranging
from the size of small dogs to specimens bigger than a man.
Most are hunters that spring at their prey and inject it with
potent venom.
LARGE SPIDER DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1/2 or 1 animal
Perception 16 (+6); darksight
Defense 14; Health 20; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 14; climber
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fangs (melee) +3 with 1 boon (1d6 plus Poison)
Poison The target must make a Strength challenge roll. On
a failure, it takes 1d6 damage and becomes poisoned
for 1 minute. If the target is already poisoned, it instead
takes 1d6 extra damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Scuttle When a creature within the spider’s reach moves,
the spider can use a triggered action to retreat.

name: LASH CRAWLER

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Lash Crawler
Clinging to walls and ceilings, lash crawlers might pass
for spiders. Close observation, though, reveals that their
bodies are bloated, pulsing eyeballs, each suspended on
seven long, hair-like legs. Lash crawlers spontaneously
appear in places scarred by reckless magic and feed on
the energy of living creatures to sustain their unnatural
existence.
Lash crawlers gather in small groups of five to ten in
caves and ruins, usually in places that have endured
bombardment from wild and chaotic magic.
LASH CRAWLER DIFFICULTY 1
Size 1/4 frightening monster
Perception 20 (+10); truesight
Defense 13; Health 5; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 8 (–2), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12; climber
ATTACK OPTIONS
Tendril (melee) +3 (1)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Warping Gaze The lash crawler makes a Will attack roll
against the Agility of one target creature it can see
within medium range of it. On a success, the target takes
1d6 damage and moves 1 yard in a direction the crawler
chooses.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Extract Eye The lash crawler uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to remove an eye from one target
defenseless creature within its reach. At the end of the
round, the eye becomes a new lash crawler.
Spring Away When a creature the lash crawler can see
gets a failure on an attack roll against the lash crawler’s
Defense or Agility, the lash crawler can use a triggered
action to retreat.

name: LESHY

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Leshy
The leshy walk the primeval forests, tending to the trees
and encouraging saplings to grow tall and strong. Leshy
dislike humans for their carelessness but despise orcs and
other filthy creatures that wantonly burn and destroy. Leshy
sometimes join forces with druids against a common enemy.
A leshy looks like a tree of any species, though oak is
most common. A leshy that stands still is indistinguishable
from a normal tree and might hold this position for
decades. When it does move, the lower trunk splits into
long legs. The leshy’s face peers out from the center of its
trunk, and it can bend its branches to use as arms.
A leshy typically speaks the Common Tongue and Elvish,
and it can communicate with any plant within 100 yards of it.
LESHY DIFFICULTY 250
Size 3 plant
Perception 15 (+5); shadowsight
Defense 20; Health 110; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 17 (+7), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 10
Immune asleep, blinded, dazed, fatigued, frightened,
stunned; a living leshy cannot be moved against its will
or knocked prone while it stands on the ground.
Fire Vulnerability A leshy takes double damage from fire.
Tree Form A leshy that does not move is indistinguishable
from an ordinary tree.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Branch (melee) +7 with 3 boons (4d6, or 24 to an object)
Boulder (long range) +7 with 2 boons (4d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The leshy attacks twice with its branch.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Awaken the Forest The leshy chooses one target tree within
medium range of it. The target becomes a compelled
monster of its size for 1 hour or until it or that leshy
becomes incapacitated. The leshy can use this action three
times. It regains expended uses after it completes a rest.

originalText:
Living Tar
Living tar is a mobile slick of black slime that creeps
toward anything it detects with its weird senses. It
gathers up its body into pseudopods with which it
smashes prey, then absorbs their vital fluids.
Some believe that living tar is the essence of slain demons
trapped in the mortal world.

---

name: LIZARDMAN

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Lizardman
Before humanity’s rise, visitors from another dimension
traveled through the Void to establish colonies in this
world. A reptilian race, with vast knowledge of magic,
science, and technology, they built cities whose ruins can
still be found in remote corners of the world or buried deep
underground. Not much is known of them or their society,
but sages speculate some calamity caused their collapse
and sent the survivors sliding into savagery. Their brutish
descendants can still be found in the bogs and swamps
of the old Empire and north, in the steaming jungles that
spread across much of that region.
Lizardmen stand about 7 feet tall and weigh around 250
pounds. Olive, brown, or black scales cover their bodies,
fading to tan on their chests. Most forgo clothing, though
warlocks in their communities sometimes wear ceremonial
robes decorated with weird glyphs and sigils.
Lizardmen speak their own language, a sibilant, hissing
tongue.
LIZARDMAN DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 lizardman
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 15 (large shield); Health 25; Insanity 3; Corruption 1
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10; swimmer
Immune frightened
Rising Fury When a lizardman takes damage, it makes its
next attack roll before the end of the next round with
1 boon.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Spear (melee) +4 with 1 boon (2d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Snapping Fangs The lizardman can use a triggered action
on its turn to bite one creature within its reach, making
a Strength attack against the target’s Defense. On a
success, the target takes 1d6 damage.

name: LURK

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Lurk
Eerie reptilian forms spring into existence and vanish just as
quickly as they hunt in the fetid waters of the swamp. Lurks
are deadly predators that use their innate magical nature to
take their prey by surprise. They appear from nowhere, rake
with their claws, and disappear in a puff of smoke.
A lurk looks like a bipedal lizard with a mottled gray-
green hide and glowing red, blue, or green spots. Two
rows of six eyes march up either side of its head, each eye
moving independently. A lurk’s forelimbs end in long,
wicked claws.
LURK DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 monster
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 40; Insanity 1; Corruption 0
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
Flickering Form Creatures make attack rolls against a lurk
with 2 banes.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws (melee) +5 with 1 boon (2d6 + 3 plus the target is
grabbed on attack roll 20+)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Void Leap The lurk uses an action or a triggered action
on its turn to disappear in a puff of acrid smoke. Any
creature grabbed by it disappears with it.
Roll a d6. On an even number, the lurk reappears in the
space it left at any time it wishes before the end of the
round. On an odd number, it reappears at the end of the
round in an open space within a number of yards of the
space it left equal to the roll. When the lurk reappears, it
makes attack rolls with 1 boon until the end of the round.
		 A creature grabbed by the lurk when it disappears
gains 1 Insanity and becomes dazed for 1 round after it
reappears.

---

name: MANES

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Manes
Death frees the mortal soul from the physical body. Souls that
sink into the Underworld become manes and pass the years in
the dark and somber place, their memories gradually fading
until nothing of their identities remains, at which point the
souls travel back to the mortal world to live again.
When a manes first appears in the Underworld, it has the
form it wore in life, albeit ashy, with dark circles around its
eyes. As the years pass, its distinctive appearance begins to
fade, leaving behind a pale, almost featureless humanoid
shape. If attacked, the manes’s fingers lengthen into claws
and its mouth yawns wide to issue an awful keening.
Manes speak the Common Tongue or High Archaic.
MANES DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1 frightening spirit
Perception 10 (+0); darksight
Defense 13; Health 20; Insanity —; Corruption 0
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 6
Immune damage from cold, disease, fire, and poison;
asleep, diseased, fatigued, immobilized, poisoned,
slowed
Eternal When a manes becomes incapacitated, it dissolves
into a puff of smoke. It re-forms in the Underworld 24
hours later with no damage.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws and Teeth (melee) +3 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)

name: MANTICORE

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Manticore
One look at a manticore is enough to know it does not belong
in this world. It has the powerful body of a red lion, with great
black wings and a scorpion’s tail that drips venom. Instead of
a lion’s head it has a monstrous human visage, twisted into a
bestial grimace. Manticores hunt and eat humans. They must
feed several times each night to appease their terrible hunger.
Many manticores learn a few words of the Common
Tongue, often those cried out by their victims in their last
moments. They mockingly parrot those words in guttural
voices as they terrorize new prey.
MANTICORE DIFFICULTY 250
Size 2 horrifying monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 16; Health 100; Insanity —; Corruption 6
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 14 (+4)
Speed 12; flier
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claw (melee) +6 with 2 boons (2d6)
Teeth (melee) +6 with 2 boons (2d6 + 1)
Stinger (melee) +6 with 2 boons (1d6 plus Poison)
Poison The target must make a Strength challenge roll with
3 banes. On a failure, it takes 5d6 damage and becomes
poisoned for 1 minute. If the target is already poisoned, it
instead takes 3d6 extra damage.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Rend The manticore attacks twice with its claw and once
with its teeth.
Swift Sting At any point during the round, the manticore
can use a triggered action to attack with its stinger.
Monster
This category comprises a variety of strange and
unnatural creatures. Some are created by Conjuration
spells, while many lurk somewhere in the wild. Monsters
usually resemble ordinary animals but have some weird
physical trait.

name: MUTTERING MAW

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Muttering Maw
Glistening trails of slime mark
the passage of muttering maws.
Purposeless, strange, and utterly
wrong, they seemingly exist only
as a remark on the perils of dabbling
with forbidden magic.
These hulking brutes are headless
but sport wide, vertical slashes down the
center of their fleshy bodies. The slick
opening is filled with rotten, brown
teeth, the gaps clotted with bits of rotting
flesh and caked with yellow-white plaque.
A muttering maw lumbers about on
elephantine legs and swings club-like
appendages ending in three-fingered
hands that grab creatures and stuff
them into its maw.
MUTTERING MAW DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 horrifying monster
Perception 14 (+4); sightless
Defense 14; Health 80; Insanity —; Corruption 3
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 8
Immune blinded
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +3 with 1 boon (2d6 plus the target is grabbed
on attack roll 20+)
Maw (melee) +3 with 1 boon (4d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Infestation of Maws The muttering maw uses an action, or
a triggered action on its turn, to create 1d6 – 2 (minimum
0) slobbering maws on solid surfaces within short range.
A maw remains for 1 minute or until the muttering maw
becomes incapacitated. When the effect ends, all the
maws disappear.
When a maw appears, and again at the end of
each round thereafter, it attempts to bite one target
creature within 1 yard of it. The target must make an
Agility challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure, it takes
1d6 damage.

name: NISSE

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Nisse
The elves withdrew from the mortal world far ahead of
humanity’s tide, but not all faerie went with them. A few
remained, unwilling to retreat to realms of dream and illusion.
Among them were the nisse, who haunt the wilderness still.
Nisse roam the frontiers of human lands, watching
mortals, weighing their actions, and judging them. In
winter, nisse might deliver gifts to human and halfling
families who have shown respect for the old ways and
ancient places, depositing tokens on their doorsteps.
A nisse looks like a tiny old man, 6 inches tall, bent with
the weight of years and hobbling with the support of a tiny
twig. It has a long white beard that drags along the ground.
Nisse wear scarlet clothing that consists of a heavy coat and a
tall, pointed cap. Some keep pigs as companions and steeds.
Nisse speak the Common Tongue and Elvish.
NISSE DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1/8 faerie
Perception 16 (+6); shadowsight
Defense 13; Health 40; Insanity 1; Corruption 0
Strength 18 (+8), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 14 (+4), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 10
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Spell Defense A nisse takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon. A
creature attacking the nisse with a spell makes the attack
roll with 1 bane.
Bigger and Bigger Each time a nisse takes damage, its Size
increases to 1 or by 1. For each point of Size above 1, the
nisse’s attacks with weapons deal 1d6 extra damage. The
nisse can use a triggered action on its turn to return to
its normal Size.
Iron Vulnerability A nisse is impaired while in contact with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Club (melee) +8 (1d6)
Teeth (melee) +8 (1 plus Gibbering Drool)
Gibbering Drool The target must make a Will challenge
roll. On a failure, it gains 1 Insanity.
MAGIC
Power 3
Illusion clamor (4), figment (2), thimblerig (2), glamer (1),
invisibility (1), phantasm (1)

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Oculus
A quivering red eye drifts across a slick of greenish-yellow
slime, reeking of sickness and disease. Visible in its
membranous body are floating scraps of skin and pieces of
bone. Oculi bubble into the world through mirrors warped
by the Demon Lord’s influence.
Dimly sentient, oculi relentlessly search for flesh to
eat. When one discovers something edible, it flows over
the prey to dissolve the meat and bones with its corrosive
secretions. Its horrific appearance can pin potential prey in
place, greatly easing the process.
OCULUS DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 horrifying monster
Perception 18 (+8); darksight
Defense 8; Health 50; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 6; Creep
Immune dazed, immobilized, prone, stunned, and any effect
that would change the oculus’s shape
Mind-Blasting Horror A creature that gains Insanity from seeing
an oculus also becomes stunned while frightened this way.
Amorphous An oculus can move freely through openings
wide enough to permit the passage of water and can
move through spaces occupied by other creatures.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Dripping Appendage (melee) +6 with 2 boons (2d6 plus
2d6 from acid)
END OF THE ROUND
Creep The oculus moves up to half its Speed. This
movement does not trigger free attacks.

originalText:
Ogre
Ogres think about little else other than the rumbling in
their prodigious bellies. They stuff their maws with what
they catch, gobbling flesh, bone, armor, dirt, and offal,
ending the meal with a thundering belch. Within moments
of eating, an ogre heads off in search of something else to
devour. Having no lands of their own, ogres wander, feed,
and then move on, leaving behind great steaming piles of
excrement.
Ogres stand about 9 feet tall. Filth crusts their mottled
and sore-dimpled hides. They drape their bodies with
rubbish they find, such as furs, tents, banners, and tarps.
They are prone to mutation and often sport all manner of
unusual physical features.
Ogres speak Trollish.
OGRE DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 ogre
Perception 7 (–3)
Defense 15; Health 80; Insanity 3; Corruption 2
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Morningstar (melee) +5 with 1 boon (2d6 + 2)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Devour The ogre eats one target defenseless or dead
creature that is Size 1 or smaller and within its reach. A
living creature dies instantly on being eaten.
Vomit When the ogre takes damage, it can use a
triggered action to vomit semidigested food into
a 3-yard-long cone originating from a point it can
reach. Each creature in the area must make an Agility
challenge roll. A creature takes 2d6 damage and
becomes impaired for 1 round on a failure, or just takes
half the damage on a success.
		 Once the ogre uses Vomit, it cannot do so again until
after it eats.

ETTIN DIFFICULTY 100

after it eats.
Though many mutations are to ogres’ detriment, the
emergence of a second head gives them an advantage.
Ogres with two heads are called ettins.

originalText:
HORNED OGRE DIFFICULTY 250
Size 3 frightening ogre
Perception 11 (+1); darksight
Defense 14; Health 100; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 18 (+8), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12
ATTACK OPTIONS
Hammer (melee) +8 with 3 boons (4d6 + 6 plus Stagger on
attack roll 20+)
Long Blade (melee) +8 with 3 boons (3d6 + 6, plus 2d6
extra damage against a dazed target)
Stagger The target becomes dazed for 1 round.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The horned ogre attacks with its hammer
and its long blade.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Devour The horned ogre eats one target defenseless or
dead creature that is Size 1 or smaller and within its
reach. A living creature dies instantly on being eaten.
Vomit When the horned ogre takes damage, it can use
a triggered action to vomit semidigested food into an
8-yard-long cone originating from a point it can reach.
Each creature in the area must make an Agility challenge
roll. A creature takes 3d6 damage and becomes impaired
for 1 round on a failure, or just takes half the damage on
a success. Once the horned ogre uses Vomit, it cannot
do so again until after it eats.
Horned ogres bear the stain of the Demon Lord’s shadow,
transformed into engines of hate and destruction. They
are both crueler and more intelligent than their smaller
fellows. They pulp their victims with massive hammers or
cut them up with their long blades before consuming them
in an orgy of gluttony.

originalText:
Ooze
Oozes are predatory slicks of transparent or translucent
slime that creep and slide across surfaces in pursuit of
prey. They feed by dissolving their prey and
absorbing nutrients from the liquefied
remains.
Oozes come in a wide variety of
colors, from gray or black to brown
to bright green, and can range in
size from harmless droplets to
pools 4 or 5 yards in diameter.

---

Bestiary
OOZE DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 to 4 ooze
Perception 14 (+4); sightless
Defense 8; Health 60; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 4; climber
Immune damage from acid; blinded, charmed, dazed,
frightened, immobilized, prone, stunned, or any effect
that would change the ooze’s shape
Split When an ooze takes damage from a weapon and the
damage does not incapacitate it, it divides. A second
ooze moves out from the original’s space into an open
space within 1 yard of it. The Size of each ooze drops by
1, and the new oozes each have Health equal to half of
the original. Each ooze has half the damage total of the
original ooze before it divided.
		 An ooze cannot divide if it is smaller than Size 1.
Amorphous An ooze can move freely through openings
wide enough to permit the passage of water, and it can
move through spaces occupied by other creatures.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Pseudopod (melee) +4 with 1 boon (3d6; no damage to
metal or stone)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Swift Attack When a creature within 1 yard of the ooze
moves, the ooze can use a triggered action to attack the
triggering creature with its pseudopod.
Elude When a creature gets a failure on an attack roll
against the ooze’s Defense or Agility, the ooze can use a
triggered action to retreat.

originalText:
Orc
Centuries ago, the Empire’s dark wizards used magic to
transform slaves into orcs, an obedient race of warriors.
The Empire relied on orcs to enforce laws and keep order
for centuries. They proved a fecund race, though, and their
numbers quickly outgrew the Empire’s ability to house
and feed them. To keep their numbers in control, orcs were
“retired” on their thirtieth birthday, shipped off to secret
camps deep underground where they were slaughtered.
Their remains, ground up into meal, fed the other orc
soldiers. Eventually they rose against their masters, and
orcs now seek their own destiny.
An orc stands about 6 feet tall and can weigh up to 300
pounds. It has pronounced bone ridges above the eyes, a
short nose, and a wide mouth filled with sharp teeth. Orcs
have blotchy skin marred with open, weeping sores, and
thick hair on their heads and faces and
across much of their bodies.
Orcs adorn themselves
with grotesque spoils of
war, such as a bundle of
severed heads hanging from
a belt, a necklace of fingers
tied around the neck, or
the faces of dead enemies
nailed to armor.
ORC DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 orc
Perception 9 (–1); shadowsight
Defense 13 (brigandine); Health 38; Insanity 2; Corruption 2
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 12
Rising Fury When an orc takes damage, it makes its next
attack roll before the end of the next round with 1 boon.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Battleaxe (melee) +3 with 1 boon (2d6 + 2)
Spear (melee or short range) +3 with 1 boon (2d6)

originalText:
Phantom
Sudden, unexpected death can leave souls anchored in
the mortal world, moored by some task left unfinished, a
loved one unguarded, or some magic whose hold cannot be
broken. Those with strong personalities become phantoms,
ghostly versions of their former selves trapped between the
realms of the living and the dead.
A phantom looks somewhat like it did in life, but its
transparent form glows faintly with eerie green light. The
true shape of its body is indistinct, with blurred edges.
Phantoms speak the Common Tongue or High Archaic.

name: POLTERGEIST

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Poltergeist
The trauma of death is only made worse when the soul
refuses to move on to the Underworld. It clings to the
mortal realm for fear of losing what it was, forgetting what
it had known, and fading from the world. Such refusal
turns to resentment for the living; when the resentment
blossoms into hate, a poltergeist results.

---

Bestiary
These “noisy ghosts” haunt places inhabited by the
living. They watch from the shadows and peer through
windows, sometimes appearing in a mirror’s reflection
or leaving a handprint on a frosty window. The longer
a poltergeist spends around the living, the angrier it
becomes until it begins trying to drive away what it sees
as intruders. A haunting begins with soft knocks, opening
and closing doors, or vile messages scrawled in dust or
chalked on the walls. If the inhabitants refuse to leave, the
poltergeist escalates the effort by hurling dishes, stacking
chairs, rearranging rooms, and more. Usually, such
displays are enough to panic the living.
It takes great effort for a poltergeist to show itself, so
it rarely does so. When it manifests, it takes the form it
had as a living person, usually sporting grievous injuries.
Poltergeists speak in whispers or communicate with
disturbing messages left in the places they haunt.
POLTERGEIST DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1/2 horrifying spirit
Perception 10 (+0); darksight
Defense 13; Health 25; Insanity —; Corruption 2
Strength —, Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 8
Immune damage from cold, disease, fire, and poison;
asleep, blinded, deafened, diseased, fatigued,
immobilized, poisoned, slowed
Insubstantial A poltergeist takes half damage from weapons,
can move through solid objects and other creatures, and
ignores the effects of moving across difficult terrain.
Naturally Invisible A poltergeist is invisible to all creatures
other than spirits, animals, and children. While invisible,
the poltergeist lacks the horrifying trait and cannot use
its attack options.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Telekinetic Slam (short range) +3 with 1 boon (1d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Hurl Object The poltergeist uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to fling one unsecured Size 1 or smaller
object within short range of it at one target creature
within medium range of it. The target must make an
Agility challenge roll with 1 bane to avoid the object.
On a failure, the creature takes 1d6 damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Manifestation The poltergeist uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to become visible. It remains visible
until it uses an action or triggered action to become
invisible once more.

name: PROMETHEAN

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Promethean
Fashioned out of body parts harvested from dead creatures
and restored to life by strange magic or weird science,
a promethean exists in a state of perpetual torment. Its
mind is assailed by memories from a life it can only dimly
remember, its sanity pushed to the breaking point by the
horror of its existence. Prometheans grudgingly serve their
makers, but if pushed too far, they might rebel, lashing out
to destroy everything around them.
Prometheans understand the Common Tongue but do
not speak.
PROMETHEAN DIFFICULTY 250
Size 2 construct
Perception 11 (+1); darksight
Defense 16; Health 140; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 18 (+8), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 10
Immune asleep, charmed, dazed, fatigued, stunned
Spell Defense A promethean takes half damage from spells
and makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon.
A creature attacking the promethean with a spell makes
the attack roll with 1 bane.
Empowered by Lightning When a promethean would take
damage from lightning, it instead adds the damage as a
bonus to its Health and makes attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 boon. These effects last for 1 minute.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +8 with 2 boons (3d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The promethean attacks twice with its fist.
END OF THE ROUND
Enrage If the promethean is not enraged, roll a d6. On a roll of
4 or higher, it becomes enraged for 1 minute. While enraged,
the promethean’s weapon attacks deal 1d6 extra damage,
and it can take both a fast turn and a slow turn each round.

---

name: REDCAP

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Redcap
The most malicious and cruel of the faerie, redcaps take
their name for the sodden hats they wear on their heads.
They drench these caps in human blood that drips and
spatters on their clothing. They must perform this ritual
and keep their caps wet or they die.
Redcaps look like little old men, gnarled and twisted,
with glittering eyes beneath beetling brows. Large yellow
teeth crowd their mouths, and streaks of blood run down
their faces and clot in their white beards. Redcaps wear
heavy boots and carry razors to slit their victims’ throats.
Redcaps speak Elvish and know a few words of the
Common Tongue.
REDCAP DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1/2 faerie
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 14; Health 20; Insanity 3; Corruption 4
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 10
Immune damage from disease; charmed, diseased
Spell Defense A redcap takes half damage from spells and
makes any challenge roll to resist a spell with 1 boon.
A creature attacking the redcap with a spell makes the
attack roll with 1 bane.
Iron Vulnerability A redcap is impaired when in contact with iron.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Razor (melee) +4 with 1 boon (1d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Speedy Boots The redcap uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to move up to four times its Speed.
Murderous Pursuit When a creature within the redcap’s
reach moves away from it, the redcap can use a
triggered action to move up to its Speed toward the
triggering creature. The redcap makes attack rolls with 1
boon against that creature for 1 round.

name: REEN

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Reen
The reen do not belong in the world. They are invaders
from another universe, one imperiled by the Demon Lord.
The people from that world dispatch reen into the Void to
locate a suitable world on which they might start again and
to prepare the way.
A reen looks like a tangle of metallic, segmented
tentacles that meet at a central ball with a single, glowing
red eye. It flies through the air or pulls itself along with its
tentacles.
Whether or not reen understand spoken languages is
unclear, since they ignore efforts to communicate with
them. They use lethal force without provocation, though
they sometimes take a moment to study their kills.
REEN DIFFICULTY 50
Size 1 construct
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 18; Health 25; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 12; climber, flier
Immune damage from disease or poison; asleep, charmed,
compelled, diseased, frightened, poisoned
Detonation When a reen becomes incapacitated, it dies
instantly and explodes. The blast extends into a 5-yard-
radius sphere centered on a point within its former
space. Everything in the area takes 3d6 damage.
Each creature in the area must make an Agility
challenge roll, taking half the damage on a
success.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Tentacle (melee; reach +2) +3 with 2 boons
(1d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Tentacle Flurry The reen flails at everything
in a 3-yard-long cone originating from a
point it can reach. Each creature in the area
must make an Agility challenge roll with 1
bane. On a failure, the creature takes 3d6
damage.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Evade and Strike When a creature
makes an attack against the reen’s
Defense or Agility, the reen can use a
triggered action to impose 1 bane on
the triggering creature’s attack roll. If
the attack misses, the reen moves up to
half its Speed and attacks the triggering
creature with its tentacle.

---

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core

originalText:
Rot Maiden
From a distance, a rot maiden looks like a seated young
woman, head down and hidden by what seems to be a
veil. Appearances are deceiving, though. A rot maiden is
actually a strange, immobile fungus that lures the unwary
to their deaths by the spores it emits. These spores have an
enticing aroma that few can resist. When a victim draws
near, the rot maiden raises its “head” and disorients its prey
with a psychic attack, then launches filaments to infect

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Shadow
A shadow is a soul bearing the stain of the Demon Lord that
slips free from the realms of the dead, sustaining its unnatural
existence by feeding on the living. Shadows loathe all life and
delight in corrupting new souls to add to their numbers.
Shadows take many forms. Some look like blots of
darkness or undulating masses of gloom. Others display
hints of who they once were in their shape and physical
characteristics, while yet others assume more monstrous
shapes that display the range of horrific traits found in
demons of the Void.
SHADOW DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 horrifying spirit
Perception 13 (+3); darksight
Defense 14; Health 20; Insanity 1; Corruption 7
Strength —, Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
Immune damage from cold, disease, fire, and poison;
asleep, blinded, deafened, diseased, fatigued,
immobilized, poisoned, slowed
Insubstantial A shadow takes half damage from weapons,
can move through solid objects and other creatures, and
ignores the effects of moving across difficult terrain.
Become the Night A shadow is invisible while in an area
obscured by shadows or darkness.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Draining Touch (melee) +4 with 2 boons (2d6 plus Drain
on attack roll 20+)
Drain A living target gains 1 Corruption and takes a –6
penalty to Health that lasts until it completes a rest.
While subject to this penalty, the target makes Strength
attack rolls and challenge rolls with 1 bane. If the target
creature becomes incapacitated by an attack a shadow
makes while the target has this penalty, the creature
dies. At the end of the next round, a new shadow
wriggles free from the body and stands up in the nearest
open space. The shadow can take the next available turn.
END OF THE ROUND
Burned by Sunlight The shadow takes 2d6 damage if it is
in an area lit by sunlight.

---

name: SHADOW WEAVER

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Shadow Weaver
Webs choke the remains of the lost city, pale strands
stretching between high towers and across the tangled
streets. Wisps of the sticky stuff hang in the air, blown
about by the fetid breeze. Such places are home to shadow
weavers, a race of intelligent spiders wholly in the thrall
of the Demon Lord. Shadow weavers hunt humans and
other sentient creatures, paralyzing them with poison
and then encasing them in sticky cocoons for later
consumption.
A shadow weaver has a glossy black body with a bulbous
abdomen. Bright red numbers glow all over the carapace,
but if these have any significance, the monsters have never
revealed it.
Shadow weavers work in small groups that follow
prey moving into their territory, creeping through
the shadows and waiting for the right time to strike.
They sometimes taunt their prisoners in Dark Speech,
whispering of the terrifying things they will do before
devouring them.
SHADOW WEAVER DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 frightening monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 16; Health 25; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 16 (+6), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10; climber
Immune immobilized, slowed
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fangs (melee) +6 (2d6 plus Corrupting Poison)
Corrupting Poison The target must make a Strength
challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure, it takes 2d6
damage, gains 1 Corruption, and becomes poisoned
for 1 minute. While poisoned this way, the target is
immobilized. If it is already poisoned, it instead takes
another 2d6 extra damage and becomes defenseless
for 1 minute.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Cocoon The shadow weaver wraps one defenseless
creature within its reach in strands of silk until the
creature becomes wholly cocooned. A cocooned
creature is immobilized until it is freed. The cocoon has
Health 10 and takes double damage from fire.
Descend The shadow weaver attaches a strand of silk to
a surface within its reach and then descends up to 10
yards on that strand. It can detach itself from the strand
at any time using a triggered action. The strand has
Health 5.
Shadow Blend When the shadow weaver moves into an
area obscured by shadows or darkness, it can use a
triggered action to automatically become hidden.

Shrieking Eel
Shrieking eels resemble ordinary eels but grow up to 12
feet long. They take their name for the alarming noise
they make when they detect prey, signaling other eels to
join the attack.
SHRIEKING EEL DIFFICULTY 10
Size 2 animal (aquatic)
Perception 12 (+2); shadowsight
Defense 13; Health 40; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 12; swimmer
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fangs (melee) +2 with 1 boon (2d6 + 2)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Shriek The eel utters a loud shriek. Until the end of the
round, each other shrieking eel within medium range of it
makes attack rolls with 1 boon.

name: SKINCHANGER

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Skinchanger
Skinchangers hide in plain sight among ordinary people,
who do not suspect their neighbor, lover, friend, or family
member bears a terrible curse. But when the moon rises
full, a change comes over the accursed one, transforming it
into a horrible monster until moonset. It becomes a wild,
savage killer, driven by an insatiable need to eat the flesh of
the living.
Skinchangers can adopt one of two other forms in
addition to their human appearance. One is that of an
animal, usually a wolf, though bears, lions, boars, giant rats,
and others are possible. In this form, the skinchanger is
physically indistinguishable from other animals of its kind,
though it behaves strangely and is unusually aggressive.
The second form is a hybrid that combines features of the
animal and humanoid shapes.
Only mortal, human-shaped creatures are susceptible to
the skinchangers’ curse—humans, halflings, dwarfs, and
the like.
SKINCHANGER DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1/2 or 1 frightening monster
Perception 13 (+3); shadowsight
Defense 15; Health 30; Insanity 4; Corruption 2
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12
Silver Vulnerability When a skinchanger takes damage
from a silver weapon, it takes a penalty to Health equal
to the damage. The penalty lasts until the skinchanger
completes a rest.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee; hybrid form only) +4 with 2 boons (3d6 plus
Skinchanger Curse)
Skinchanger Curse If the target is human or a similar
mortal creature and becomes incapacitated by the
skinchanger’s attack but does not die, it must make a
Strength challenge roll with 1 bane the next time the
moon rises full. On a failure, the target transforms into
a skinchanger until moonset. While transformed, it uses
the skinchanger’s attributes, characteristics, attacks,
talents, and traits in place of its own but can take only
hybrid form. When the transformation ends, the target
has no memory of its time as a skinchanger.
		 The curse lasts until lifted or until the target kills the
skinchanger that cursed it.

---

Bestiary
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Change Form The skinchanger uses an action or a
triggered action on its turn to assume the form of a
medium animal, assume a hybrid form, or return to its
human form. While in animal form, it uses that creature’s
physical attributes, characteristics, attacks, talents, and
traits. It retains its own Intellect and Will.
END OF THE ROUND
Regeneration The skinchanger heals 1d6 damage if it is not
incapacitated.

originalText:
Spriggan
People who explore the borders between the mortal world
and the hidden kingdoms of the faerie sometimes report
encountering strange, violent folk of the wood that attack
without provocation and seem intent on driving interlopers
away. These beings are spriggans, magical creations of the
Fair Folk tasked with protecting their borders and places
important to their kind.
A spriggan stands about 5 feet tall and has a willowy,
humanoid shape made from twisting vines and thorny
branches. It has sparse facial features, little more than a
pair of glowing green eyes.
Spriggans understand Elvish but do not speak.
SPRIGGAN DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 plant
Perception 15 (+5); shadowsight
Defense 16; Health 50; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 12; climber
Immune asleep, blinded, dazed, fatigued, frightened,
stunned
Fire Vulnerability A spriggan takes double damage from fire.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claw (melee) +4 with 2 boons (2d6)
Thorn (medium range) +4 with 1 boon (2d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Thorny Vine A vine rises from the ground and attacks one
target creature within medium range of the spriggan.
The target must make an Agility challenge roll with 1
bane. On a failure, it takes 1d6 damage and becomes
immobilized until the spriggan dies. If the target is
already immobilized, it instead takes 2d6 extra damage.
		 A creature immobilized this way can use an action to
make a Strength challenge roll. A success ends the affliction.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Camouflage If the spriggan is covered or in an area
obscured by foliage or natural terrain features and is not
being observed, it can use an action or a triggered action
on its turn to automatically become hidden.

name: STONE WORM

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Stone Worm
Stone worms burrow through the earth, surfacing to snatch
livestock or people and drag them into the subterranean
darkness. A profusion of deep craters mark places infested
with these relentless hunters. From the depths rises the
stench of rotting meat mingled with an odd cinnamon smell.
A stone worm can grow up to 24 feet long and have a
diameter of up to 6 feet. Its segmented body has a thick,
rubbery hide, mottled brown and gray. Thin slime oozes
from the creases between the segments and a great,
yawning maw dominates its scarred head, filled with sharp,
inward-pointing teeth.
STONE WORM DIFFICULTY 50
Size 2 or 3 monster
Perception 11 (+1); sightless
Defense 18; Health 30; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 8; Tunnel
Immune blinded
ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee) +6 (4d6 plus Swallow on attack roll 20+)
Swallow If the target is smaller than the stone worm, it
must make an Agility challenge roll with 1 bane. On a
failure, the target is swallowed.
		 A swallowed creature is defenseless, moves with the
worm, and cannot perceive anything outside the worm’s
body. At the end of each round, the swallowed creature
takes 2d6 damage from the worm’s digestive juices. If
the worm becomes incapacitated, it vomits forth any
creatures it has swallowed. Each lands prone in an open
space within 1 yard of the worm.

---

Bestiary
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Vomit The stone worm vomits digestive juices and
anything it swallowed into a 5-yard-long cone originating
from a point it can reach. Everything in the area takes
6d6 damage, or half the damage with a successful Agility
challenge roll.
		 Any creatures the worm had swallowed prior to
making this attack are expelled, landing prone in an
open space within 1 yard of the worm. They make Agility
challenge rolls against this attack with 1 bane. Once the
stone worm uses Vomit, it cannot do so again for 1 hour.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Tunnel The stone worm moves up to its Speed through
earth, sand, or other material of similar consistency. It
leaves a 1-yard-diameter tunnel behind it.
