source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Stranglevine
From bright yellow flowers dotting these masses of
vegetation comes sweet odors living creatures find
intoxicating. The stranglevines lure such creatures close
with the perfume, and then use their vines to strangle and
crush their victims’ bodies. The plants then feed on the
nutrients that leak from rotting corpses.
STRANGLEVINE DIFFICULTY 50
Size 5 plant
Perception 15 (+5); sightless
Defense 15; Health 40; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 6 (–4), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 1
Immune asleep, blinded, dazed, fatigued, frightened,
stunned
Fire Vulnerability A stranglevine takes double damage
from fire.
Intoxicating Scent The stranglevine fills the air out to long
range from it with a powerful scent. A living creature
that enters the area or starts its turn there must make a
Strength challenge roll.
		 On a failure, the creature becomes dazed for 1 round.
While dazed this way, the creature is also impaired
and can take only fast turns to rush toward the nearest
stranglevine by the shortest available route.
		 On a success, the creature becomes immune to that
stranglevine’s Intoxicating Scent until that creature
completes a rest.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Vines (melee) +4 with 2 boons (1d6 + 2, plus the target is
grabbed on attack roll 20+)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Storm of Vines The stranglevine attacks four times with its
vines.

name: TOMB SCARAB SWARM

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Tomb Scarab Swarm
Tomb scarabs are beetles that infest the ruins of the
Desolation. When they sense prey, they gather into great,
heaving swarms that can strip a living creature down to
bone in a matter of seconds. Each scarab has a crimson
stripe running down the center of its shell.
TOMB SCARAB SWARM DIFFICULTY 25
Size 1 animal (swarm)
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 17; Health 30; Insanity —; Corruption 0
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12; climber
Immune charmed, dazed, deafened, frightened, grabbed,
immobilized, prone, slowed, stunned
Multitude A swarm takes half damage from attacks that
use an attack roll and double damage from effects that
require it to make a challenge roll.
Revulsion Creatures that are not swarms are impaired while
they remain in the swarm’s space or within 1 yard of it.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Mandibles (melee) +3 with 1 boon (2d6 plus Invasion, or
just 1d6 if the swarm is injured)
Invasion If living, the target must make a Strength
challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure, the swarm
burrows into its body, dealing 4d6 extra damage, and
then exits into an open space within 1 yard of the target.
If the target becomes incapacitated by this damage, it
dies instantly, the flesh (if any) stripped from its bones.
END OF THE ROUND
Swarming Scarabs Each creature that isn’t a swarm that is
in the swarm’s space or within 1 yard of it must make an
Agility challenge roll. On a failure, the creature takes 2d6
damage and becomes slowed for 1 round.

name: TROGLODYTE

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Troglodyte
Troglodytes abandoned their humanity when they fled into
the bowels of the earth to escape justice for their wicked
acts. They survived for generations in the noisome dark,
becoming more and more inbred until they were reduced to
a gibbering mob.
Troglodytes have hairless, chalk-white skin crusted with
filth and blood. Bruises ring their black eyes, and they
file their teeth to sharp points. They rarely bother to wear
clothing and instead paint their bodies with white mud.
Troglodytes speak a debased form of High Archaic
peppered with words and phrases from Dark Speech.
TROGLODYTE DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1 frightening troglodyte
Perception 12 (+2); darksight
Defense 10; Health 30; Insanity 4; Corruption 3
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 12
Sunlight Weakness A troglodyte is impaired while in an
area lit by sunlight.
Strength from Pain While the troglodyte is injured, it
makes attack rolls with 1 boon and its weapon attacks
deal 1d6 extra damage.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Pick (melee) +3 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The troglodyte can attempt to hide when
it is in an area at least partially obscured by shadows,
even if it is being observed.

---

Bestiary

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Troll
Trolls have lived in the world almost as long as the faerie.
A hateful, spiteful race, they despise the Fair Folk for their
beauty, mischief, and joy. In ancient times, they fought
bloody, disastrous wars against their foes until the Faerie
Queen, sickened by the carnage, stripped them of their
magic and left them vulnerable to the sun’s purifying light.
The accursed trolls retreated to deep valleys and dug into
caves under mountains and hills to escape the hateful light.
Thus began their rapid decline into madness and savagery,
until they became little more than lumbering brutes filled
with a dim hatred for all living things.
A typical troll stands 10 feet tall and weighs 750 pounds.
It has a stooped body, a bulbous nose, and a wide mouth
filled with chisel-like teeth. Most trolls have patches of
petrified flesh from brief encounters with the sun. They
wear animal hides as clothing.
All trolls speak Trollish, and most know a little Elvish
and the Common Tongue.
TROLL DIFFICULTY 250
Size 2 troll
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 16; Health 110 (Regeneration); Insanity 1; Corruption 3
Strength 18 (+8), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 10 (+0)
Speed 8
Hatred During the first round of combat, a troll makes all
attack rolls with 1 boon.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Fist (melee) +8 with 3 boons (4d6 plus Grab and Bite on
attack roll 20+)
Grab and Bite If the target is smaller than the troll, it takes
4d6 damage and falls prone in a space the troll chooses
within the troll’s reach.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The troll attacks twice with its fist.
END OF THE ROUND

evidence.excerpt:
Troll
Trolls have lived in the world almost as long as the faerie.
A hateful, spiteful race, they despise the Fair Folk for their
beauty, mischief, and joy. In ancient times, they fought
bloody, disastrous wars against their foes until the Faerie
Queen, sickened by the carnage, stripped them of their
magic and left them vulnerable to the sun’s purifying light.
The accursed trolls retreated to deep valleys and dug into
caves under mountains and hills to escape the hateful light.
Thus began their rapid decline into madness and savagery,
until they became little more than lumbering brutes filled
with a dim hatred for all living things.
A typical troll stands 10 feet tall and weighs 750 pounds.
It has a stooped body, a bulbous nose, and a wide mouth
filled with chisel-like teeth. Most trolls have patches of
petrified flesh from brief encounters with the sun. They
wear animal hides as clothing.
All trolls speak Trollish, and most know a little Elvish
and the Common Tongue.
TROLL DIFFICULTY 250

Defense 16; Health 110 (Regeneration); Insanity 1; Corruption 3

within the troll’s reach.

incapacitated.

originalText:
Vampire
Vampires rule the night. When the sun sinks beneath the
horizon, they emerge from their tombs to stalk the living,
drawing them close with magic and draining their blood.
Vampires possess great power but have several fatal flaws that
bold hunters can exploit. For this reason, vampires show great
restraint even though they constantly thirst for fresh blood.
A vampire can create a “child” by draining a victim to the
point that it starts dying. It feeds the creature some of the
vampire’s own blood, killing the victim almost immediately,
then inters the corpse in a tomb, vault, coffin, or somewhere
else the sun cannot reach. The corpse rises as a new
vampire at the next sunset and is compelled until released
or until its maker is destroyed.
The process of becoming undead leaves a vampire
somewhat unhinged, and many develop irrational
superstitions. They might recoil from mirrors, compulsively
count everything they see, be repulsed by the stench of
garlic, or retreat from a brandished holy symbol. None of
these things cause real harm to a vampire and, in time, it
might overcome its superstition.
Vampires speak High Archaic and the Common Tongue.
VAMPIRE DIFFICULTY 250
Size 1 horrifying undead
Perception 16 (+6); darksight
Defense 20; Health 90; Insanity —; Corruption 5
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 14 (+4), Will 16 (+6)
Speed 14
Immune damage from cold, disease, poison; asleep,
diseased, fatigued, immobilized, poisoned, slowed
Resilience A vampire takes half damage from weapons.
Celestial Vulnerability A vampire takes double damage
from Celestial spells and makes challenge rolls to resist
Celestial spells with 1 bane.
Fear of the Gods A vampire makes attack rolls with 1 bane
against a creature wearing or wielding a holy symbol.
Pass for Human A vampire appears human until it takes
damage or makes an attack roll, at which point its
features contort to assume a monstrous appearance. The
vampire retains this appearance until it uses an action to
resume its human appearance. While it appears human,
the vampire loses its horrifying trait.

---

Bestiary
ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws (melee) +5 with 3 boons (2d6 plus the target is
grabbed on attack roll 20+)
Fangs (melee) +5 with 1 boon (3d6)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Double Attack The vampire attacks twice with its claws.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Blood Drain The vampire makes a Strength attack roll
against the Strength of one target living creature of
flesh and blood that it is grabbing. On a success, the
target takes 3d6 damage and becomes fatigued until it
completes a rest. The vampire heals the same amount
of damage. If the target is already fatigued this way, it
must make a Will challenge roll. On a failure, it instead
becomes charmed until it completes a rest.
Flowing Mist When the vampire takes damage, it can use
a triggered action to turn its body into mist, fly up to its
Speed, and then resume its normal form. While in mist
form, it is immune to all damage, its movement does not
trigger free attacks, and it can move through openings
wide enough to permit the passage of air and through
spaces occupied by other creatures.
END OF THE ROUND
Burned by Sunlight The vampire takes 2d6 damage if it is
in an area lit by sunlight.

originalText:
Vampire Bat
Vampire bats are large, fast, and deadly predators, as quick
on the ground as they are flying through the air. They
scurry after prey, leaping to sink their fangs into the meat
and gulp the hot blood spraying from the wound.
VAMPIRE BAT DIFFICULTY 10
Size 1/2 animal
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 15; Health 20; Insanity 0; Corruption 0
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 15 (+5), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12; flier (swoop)
ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee) +5 (1d6 + 1 plus Bleed or Blood Drain)
Bleed If living, the target must make a Strength challenge
roll. On a failure, it becomes fatigued for 1 minute or until
it heals any damage. At the end of each round while
fatigued this way, it takes 1 damage.
Blood Drain The vampire bat makes a Strength attack roll
against the Agility of the target. On a success, the target
is grabbed and takes 1d6 extra damage if it is living.

originalText:
Void Larva
In places where the boundaries between the world and
the Void have grown thin, the land becomes stained by the
demonic leakage, spawning manifestations of its dread
nature as wriggling larvae. These fleshy monstrosities look
like enormous grubs with rubbery pink skin. Sharp teeth
ring their circular maws, from which runs corrosive slime
that liquefies whatever it touches.
VOID LARVA DIFFICULTY 1
Size 1/4 frightening demon
Perception 5 (–5); sightless
Defense 8; Health 10; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 5 (–5)
Speed 6
Immune blinded
ATTACK OPTIONS
Dripping Teeth (melee) +1 with 2 boons (1d6 plus 1d6 from acid)
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Spit Acid The void larva spits corrosive slime at one target
creature or object within short range of it. The larva
makes an Agility attack roll against the target’s Agility.
On a success, the target takes 1d6 + 2 damage.

originalText:
Wraith
Souls in Hell sometimes slip free to visit evil and suffering
on the world. A wraith resembles a human-shaped blot of
darkness. Crimson lights burns where the eyes ought to be.
Wraiths understand High Archaic and the Common
Tongue, though they rarely speak.
WRAITH DIFFICULTY 100
Size 1 horrifying spirit
Perception 14 (+4); darksight
Defense 16; Health 60; Insanity —; Corruption 6
Strength —, Agility 16 (+6), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 14 (+4)
Speed 14; flier
Immune damage from cold, disease, fire, and poison;
asleep, diseased, fatigued, immobilized, poisoned,
slowed
Insubstantial A wraith takes half damage from weapons,
can move through solid objects and other creatures, and
ignores the effects of moving across difficult terrain.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Shadow Blade (melee) +6 with 2 boons (2d6 and Lasting Harm)
Lasting Harm A living target takes a cumulative penalty to
Health equal to the damage taken from the attack. If the
target creature becomes incapacitated by an attack a

---

Bestiary
wraith makes while the target has this penalty, it dies. At
the end of the next round, a new wraith with half the Health
of its creator wriggles free from the body and stands up in
the nearest open space. The wraith is compelled for 1 hour
by its creator, after which time it can act normally.
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Ethereal Wind The wraith uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to move up to its Speed. This movement
does not trigger free attacks.
END OF THE ROUND
Burned by Sunlight The wraith takes 3d6 damage if it is in
an area lit by sunlight.

name: ZOMBIE

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Zombie
Herds of shuffling corpses, driven by an insatiable hunger for
flesh, roam the countryside, created by a plague infused with
dark magic from the corpses of the recently dead. Zombies
bear the grisly marks that ended their lives, and make do with
split bellies with entrails hanging free, broken limbs, and
worse. They spread their foul disease through their bites.
ZOMBIE DIFFICULTY 5
Size 1/2 or 1 frightening undead
Perception 10 (+0); shadowsight
Defense 9; Health 20; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 8; Shuffling Advance
Immune damage from disease and poison; gaining Insanity;
asleep, charmed, dazed, diseased, fatigued, frightened,
poisoned, stunned
Headshot When the total of an attack roll with a weapon
against a zombie is 20 or higher, the zombie takes damage
equal to its Health instead of the weapon’s normal damage.
Sluggish The zombie cannot use triggered actions. When the
zombie takes a turn, it can either use an action or move up to
its Speed, regardless of when it takes its turn during the round.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee) +1 with 1 boon (1d6 + 1 plus Zombie Plague);
the zombie makes the attack roll with 1 boon against a
grabbed creature.
Zombie Plague If the target is human or a human-like creature,
it must make a Strength challenge roll. On a failure, the target
becomes diseased. While it is diseased this way, the target
cannot heal damage and makes attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane. If it becomes incapacitated while diseased
this way, it dies instantly and rises up as a new zombie
1d6 rounds later. Each time a creature diseased this way
completes a rest, it must make a Strength challenge roll. On a
failure, the creature takes a 1d6 penalty to Health. The penalty
lasts until this diseased affliction is removed. If this penalty
reduces the creature’s Health to 0 while it is diseased this
way, it dies and rises as a zombie 1d6 rounds later. After three
successes, the creature removes this diseased affliction.
SPECIAL ATTACKS
Grasping Hands The zombie makes a Strength attack roll
with 1 boon against the Agility of one target creature
within its reach. On a success, the target takes 1d3
damage and becomes grabbed.
END OF THE ROUND
Shuffling Advance The zombie moves 1d3 yards toward
the nearest living creature.
Characters
In addition to the creatures described here, player
characters might encounter other people, many of whom
can be just as dangerous as monsters. All the characters
described in this section are assumed to be human, though
they can have any ancestry you want without significantly
altering their statistics.
Characters speak the languages of their homelands.
Educated characters might also read and write one or
more languages.
Acolyte of the New God
Acolytes of the New God travel the lands of the Empire,
working to combat corruption’s spread and fight agents
sworn to the Demon Lord.
ACOLYTEOFTHENEWGOD DIFFICULTY5
Size ½ or 1 human
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 17 (mail, large shield); Health 20
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Mace (melee) +3 (1d6)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Prayer When a creature within short range of the acolyte
makes a challenge roll or an attack roll, the acolyte can use
a triggered action to grant 1 boon to the triggering roll.
MAGIC
Power 2
Life minor healing (2), cure (1), vitality burst (1)
Theurgy denounce (2), blessing (1)

Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS

surprised target)

name: BRIGAND

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Brigand
Brigands terrorize the countryside. They seek out isolated
homes and farmsteads, kicking in doors and brutalize anyone
they find inside. After killing their victims, they take anything
of value and light the place on fire. Brigands may be former
soldiers, tough individuals fallen on hard times, or just cruel
and wicked people exploiting the present difficulties to take
what they want without fear of repercussion.
BRIGAND DIFFICULTY 10
Size ½ or 1 human
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 15 (brigandine, large shield); Health 15
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Sword (melee) +3 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)
Crossbow (long range) +1 with 1 boon (2d6)
Commoner/Professional
Commoners and professionals include beggars and
blacksmiths, porters and laborers, servants, and most other
people the characters might encounter in their daily lives.
COMMONER OR PROFESSIONAL DIFFICULTY1
Size ½ or 1 human
Perception 9 (–1)
Defense 10; Health 11
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Staff (melee) +1 (1d6 + 1)
Dagger (melee or short range) +1 (1d3)

name: CULTIST

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Cultist
In uncertain times, some people look for divine beings
to ease their fears and grant them hope that they will
somehow survive the catastrophes ravaging their lives. Most
turn to the established religions, finding comfort in the
Cult of the New God or a place among the devotees of the
Old Faith. But some turn to darker, more sinister powers for
succor.
Cultists include any groups of like-minded individuals
pledged to serve a mysterious power that might or might
not be a god. Many cults, in fact, venerate the Demon Lord
in one of its many aspects without realizing their work
advances the aims of this terrifying power.
Most cultists speak the Common Tongue.
CULTIST DIFFICULTY 1
Size ½ or 1 human
Perception 9 (–1)
Defense 10; Health 11
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 8 (–2)
Speed 10
Mad Certainty When a cultist makes a challenge roll or an
attack roll, it can make the roll with 1 boon. On a failure,
the cultist takes 1d6 damage.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Sickle (melee) +1 (1d6)

name: HIGH CULTIST

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
High Cultist
At the center of every cult stands a high cultist, the leader of
the deranged band. Such individuals usually possess strong
and magnetic personalities that attract the weak-willed
and unstable. High cultists possess true power, sometimes
gained by bargaining with devils or from encounters with
demonic relics, and they use that power to impress, coerce,
and corrupt the people who follow them.

---

Bestiary
HIGH CULTIST DIFFICULTY 50
Size ½ or 1 human
Perception 14 (+4)
Defense 13; Health 50
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 14 (+4), Will 8 (–2)
Speed 10
ATTACK OPTIONS
Staff (melee) +3 (1d6 + 1)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Necessary Sacrifice One target cultist within short range of
the high cultist that is friendly to it takes damage equal
to the cultist’s Health. The high cultist regains the casting
of one spell and may cast it immediately.
MAGIC
Power 2
Forbidden harm (3), obedience (2), vision’s end (1)

interference.

roll.

name: PICKPOCKET

source.rawLabel: Shadow of the Demon Lord Core
source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Pickpocket
Pickpockets work the streets, lifting small items as they
move. Most prey on the wealthy, favoring merchants,
nobles, and the like over the poor and downtrodden. Many
pickpockets belong to the community’s organized crime
syndicate if one exists.
PICKPOCKET DIFFICULTY 10
Size ½ or 1 human
Perception 12 (+2)
Defense 13 (soft leather); Health 16
Strength 10 (+0), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 10
Trickery Once per round, the pickpocket can make a
challenge roll or an attack roll with 1 boon.
ATTACK OPTIONS
Small Sword (melee) +2 (1d6, plus 1d6 if the pickpocket
had 1 boon from Trickery)
Dagger (melee or short range) +2 (1d3, plus 1d6 if the
pickpocket had 1 boon from Trickery)
SPECIAL ACTIONS
Threats The pickpocket uses an action or a triggered
action on its turn to make an Intellect attack roll against
the Will of one target creature within short range of
it that can hear and see it. On a success, the target
becomes frightened for 1 round. On a failure, the target
becomes immune to that pickpocket’s Threats for 24
hours.
